title: Recognise Engram's terminal control-startup codes (control_startup_busy, control_startup_refused): evict the worker, re-admit on busy, fail closed on refused
outcome:
Engram proposes two reserved terminal control-startup codes, in the existing strict envelope {"status":"error","error":{"code","message"}}: control_startup_busy and control_startup_refused. Each is one flushed JSON line answering the first frame, followed by a nonzero exit. TermAl's reader must land FIRST or together with Engram's producer.
TermAl recognises both as TERMINAL remote errors. It discards and reaps the cached control worker; the generic 'keep every Remote process alive' rule (engram_host_adapter.rs ~1013-1014 at 3a8b7f9c) must not apply to them. Busy is retry-eligible only through the safe re-admission, status and rebind machinery, on w-7224e6317e55's common schedule. Refused fails closed, like a fatal disabled_reason.
Neither code is treated as process_never_started or as 'no durable mutation'. No blind replay of a possibly executed request, and no generic reopen around resume-nonce rotation. Healthy-frame storage_error replies keep their current meaning. Tests cover: each code evicting the worker; busy re-admitted on the schedule; refused held; and an unknown code still handled as today.
acceptance: TermAl classifies Engram's control_startup_busy and control_startup_refused, matched on the error code only, as terminal remote errors: the control worker that returned one is evicted and reaped, and a later call starts a new worker; neither is treated as process-never-started or as certified non-application. A live storage_error and unknown codes keep their worker as before. Tests cover each code's eviction with a real fixture process and the unchanged cases.

control_startup_busy re-enters only the existing safe re-admission (replay of the exact retained request and key, with status and rebind as the existing recovery requires) on the common recovery schedule and is delivered once on recovery; control_startup_refused fails closed like a fatal disabled_reason, holding the retained prompt with nothing sent automatically. Tests cover busy on evaluate and on bind, refused held, and an unknown code handled as today.
The full five-stage gate passes on the exact committed tree, and an independent Codex plus Claude read-only review pair has no outstanding in-scope Medium-or-higher finding.
